{{Top}}
{{MultipleIssues|updatecontent=[[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope]], [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back]], [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi]], [[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]], [[Red Harvest (novel)|Red Harvest]], [[Star Wars: The Old Republic]], [[Darth Plagueis (novel)|Darth Plagueis]], [[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side]], [[Destiny (The Clone Wars)|Destiny]]}}
{{Quote|There is no Death, there is the Force|The [[Jedi Code/Legends|Jedi Code]]|<ref name="BoS">''[[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Immortal.jpg|thumb|right|333px|The immortal Force Priestess Serenity]]
'''Immortality''' was the state of living eternally, being [[Death/Legends|deathless]].<ref name="SoR">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Shadow of Revan]]''</ref> The goal of many [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] beings throughout [[Timeline of galactic history/Legends|galactic history]], the state of immortality was attainable by few.<ref name="BoS">''[[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side]]''</ref>

Such individuals were calm and centered; at peace and existing in the present&mdash;in tune with the [[Living Force/Legends|Living Force]]. Only through this, known as the [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light side of the Force]],<ref name="Sacrifice">{{TCW|Sacrifice (episode)}}</ref> were individuals able to let go of their physical body, becoming one with [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] and [[Force ghost/Legends|manifesting their consciousness]] in order to commune with the living after death through the [[Cosmic Force/Legends|Cosmic Force]].<ref name="Voices">{{TCW|Voices}}</ref>

Individuals fearful of their own end may turn to seek immortality, drawn to become obsessive for eternal life in their lust for power.<ref name="BoS" /> Such individuals who were naturally [[Force-sensitive/Legends|highly attuned]] to the Force through high quantities of [[Midi-chlorian/Legends|midi-chlorians]] in their [[Blood/Legends|blood]]&mdash;which formed a symbiote with their host as the microscopic life forms spoke the will of the Force<ref name="TPM">{{Film|I}}</ref>&mdash;were consumed by indulging in emotions such as fear and hate in their attempts for immortality;<ref name="An Unthinkable Alliance">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Knight|An Unthinkable Alliance|the Emperor's Fortress}}</ref> forcefully [[Force power/Legends|tapping into the Force]]<ref name="BoS" /> through their own<ref name="Plagueis">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref>&mdash;and in certain cases, others'&mdash;midi-chlorians.<ref name="Red Harvest">[[Red Harvest (novel)|''Red Harvest'']]</ref> Known as becoming chained to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]], all who took this path, many a [[Sith/Legends|Sith]], perished as a result of attempting to amalgamating and hoarding power for immortality.<ref name="BoS" />

However, phantoms of these dark side menaces existed. These spectres of the past haunted lost, lifeless lands, such as the [[Valley of the Dark Lords/Legends|tombs of Korriban]].<ref name="Tales">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith 2|''Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith'' 2]]</ref> Preserved in physical objects, such as the [[Muur Talisman]] and [[Rakata/Legends|Rakata]] [[mind prison]]s, vengeful spirits seeped out of their cages, always attempting to latch themselves onto a living body, hoping to take control of other life forms and accumulate power without end.<ref name="Vector 6">[[Dark Times 12|''Dark Times'' 12]]</ref><ref name="KOTOR">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]''</ref>

[[File:TestOfTheOne-Overlords.png|thumb|left|332px|The dichotomy between the light and dark was a significant recurrence in galactic history.]]
With such constant looming threats against all of life,<ref name="Vector 6" /><ref name="SoR" /> the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]], servants of the Force in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], sought to bring [[Balance/Legends|balance]]; maintaining and restoring harmony among the Living Force.<ref name="TPM" /> Through great sacrifice, balance was achievable, and with peace and purpose, one could retain their consciousness after death and also achieve immortality to continue giving to the living.<ref name="BoS" /><ref name="Heir">''[[Heir to the Empire]]''</ref> Even without achieving this state, most Jedi tended to live longer than average members of their race due to their connection with the Force, 

Although threats of power-hungry individuals recurred,<ref name="Apocalypse">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Apocalypse]]''</ref> it was through the teachings of the immortal that newer generations learned, grew, and overthrow their darkness;<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref><ref name="ESB">{{Film|V}}</ref><ref name="ROTJ">{{Film|VI}}</ref> there was a cyclical nature between the dichotomy of light and dark.<ref name="Apocalypse" /><ref name="BoS" />

==History==
*The [[Gorach]] [[Species/Legends|species]] was thought to have a biological immortal lifespan, living for thousands of [[Standard year/Legends|years]], and only [[Death/Legends|dying]] through violent means.<ref name="INS133">{{InsiderCite|133|Hunting the Gorach}}</ref> Similarly, the [[Diathim/Legends|Diathim]] and [[Maelibus]] races were believed to be immortal.
*The Force-wielder known as [[Abeloth]], as well as her "[[The Ones/Legends|family]]" were immortal, only facing death when killed, and her family could only be killed by the [[Dagger of Mortis/Legends|Dagger of Mortis]].
*[[Orgus Din]] became an immortal [[Force ghost/Legends|Force ghost]] after his death at the hands of [[Darth Angral]].
*[[Set Harth]] cheated death by using [[essence transfer]] on clone bodies, and thus lived for at least a thousand years.<ref name="UA">''[[Ultimate Adversaries]]''</ref>
*[[The Imprisoned One]] attempted to secure his own immortality by use of the Force and nanotechnology but was branded a heretic by the Rakata and imprisoned in a Rakata [[mind prison]] before he could do so.<ref name="nanotech">{{TORcite|type=faction|[[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]]|The Thing Czerka Found|[[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]}}</ref>
*[[Karness Muur]], with the help of [[Sorzus Syn]], created the [[Muur Talisman]] and upon his death transferred his consciousness into it, allowing his spirit and mind to survive until its final destruction, four thousand years later.<ref name="Book of Sith">''[[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side]]''</ref>
*[[Darth Andeddu]] created the essence transfer ability which essentially was a form of immortality.<ref name="DOE">''[[Darth Bane: Dynasty of Evil]]''</ref> He was able to return to life in [[137 ABY]] when he drained his servant's spirit back into his corpse.<ref name="Legacy 27">[[Legacy (2006) 27|''Legacy'' (2006) 27]]</ref>
*[[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Tenebrae|Vitiate]] was a [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] who successfully gained near immortality by draining the life force of an entire planet, later attempting to drain all life in the galaxy, which would give him true immortality. After killing the planet [[Ziost/Legends|Ziost]], he focused all his attention on his second life as the "Immortal Emperor," [[Tenebrae|Valkorion]] of Zakuul. When he was killed in a battle against his son, he left his body and entered [[Alliance Commander|The Outlander]]. When the Outlander was frozen in carbonite, Valkorion spoke to them, claiming that he had finally reached true immortality by shedding his body, and living as a Force entity.
*[[Scourge (Sith)|Lord Scourge]] gained immortality as the [[Emperor's Wrath|right hand]] servant of Emperor Vitiate. However, this promotion came with a heavy price: although feeling excruciating pain at first he would eventually become numb and stop feeling anything at all.<ref name="TORR">''[[The Old Republic: Revan]]''</ref>
*[[Celeste Morne]] became the wielder of the [[Muur Talisman]] to contain its power. While initially placed in stasis, upon awakening she tapped its power and in the process learned to use it to the extent that she remained unaged for over a hundred and forty years.<ref name="Dark Times 12">[[Dark Times 12|''Dark Times'' 12]]</ref><ref name="Legacy31">[[Legacy (2006) 31|''Legacy'' (2006) 31]]</ref>
*[[Darth Sion]] achieved the ability to rise from near-fatal injuries through sheer hatred. However, it left him a broken shell of accumulated injuries and wounds.<ref name="TSL">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]''</ref>
*[[Darth Drear]] thought to cheat death by infecting himself with the [[Imperial bioweapons Project I71A|Sickness]] and then feasting on the heart of a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]], having the [[Midi-chlorian/Legends|midi-chlorians]] stabilize his condition. This method failed, but only because Drear could not find a victim strong enough in [[The Force/Legends|the Force]].<ref name="RH">[[Red Harvest (novel)|''Red Harvest'']]</ref>
*[[Darth Zash]] sought to avoid death by using several artifacts created by [[Tulak Hord]] that when used in a unique ritual could allow one's essence to travel to another vessel. She looked for an apprentice who'd be able to find the artifacts and then take over their body. Although successful, her essence was instead transferred into a [[Dashade/Legends|Dashade's]] body named [[Khem Val]] which she shared with him.<ref name="STOR">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''</ref>
*[[Darth Bane/Legends|Darth Bane]] attempted to transfer his [[Force ghost/Legends|spirit]] into another vessel because of the increasingly decrepit condition of his body, which had been physically drained after years of harnessing the [[Force power/Legends|power]] of the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]]. Although he originally groomed [[Darth Zannah/Legends|Darth Zannah]] as his [[Sith apprentice/Legends|heir]], Bane came to believe that she was ultimately unworthy to take up the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord's]] mantle. Thus, he sought to preserve his life in order to [[Sith training|train]] a new apprentice. His plot ultimately failed when Zannah confronted and killed her [[Sith Master/Legends|Master]] in [[Duel on Ambria (980 BBY)|combat]].<ref name="DOE" />
*[[Darth Tenebrous/Legends|Darth Tenebrous]] achieved a form of immortality that backfired horribly on him. By converting his consciousness into a new kind of midi-chlorians known as [[maxi-chlorian]]s, he was seemingly forced to live his final moments for all eternity in an infinite time loop, unless his maxi-chlorians ever died.<ref name="The Tenebrous Way">{{InsiderCite|130|The Tenebrous Way}}</ref>
*[[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Darth Plagueis]] discovered immortality through [[Midi-chlorian manipulation]]. Nevertheless, he was unable to prevent his own death in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]] at the hands of his apprentice [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]].<ref name="SWDP">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref>
*[[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Fay]] remained youthful for centuries through her deep connection to the Force. [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] believed that she would have lived forever if she hadn't sacrificed herself to help him on [[Queyta]].<ref name="Blast Radius">[[Republic 53|''Republic'' 53]]</ref>
*[[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] learned to manifest as a [[Force ghost/Legends|Force ghost]] after death, thus allowing him to retain his consciousness in the Force.<ref name="ROTSn">[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode III: Revenge of the Sith'' (novel)]]</ref> Several other Jedi also achieved the same ability, most notably Obi-Wan Kenobi,<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref> [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]] and the redeemed [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]].<ref name="ROTJ">{{Film|VI}}</ref> Some Sith employed similar techniques with varying levels of success.<ref name="JvS" />
*[[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]] intended to [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|rule]] [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] for eternity after he rediscovered the lost Force technique known as essence transfer.<ref name="JvS">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref> Using himself as a [[DNA/Legends|genetic]] [[Clone template/Legends|template]], Sidious secretly commissioned a batch of<ref name="DE2">[[Dark Empire 2|''Dark Empire'' 2]]</ref> [[Spaarti cloning cylinder|growth-accelerated]]<ref name="JvS" /> [[Cloning/Legends|clones]]. Each clone was intended to serve as a temporary vessel for the Dark Lord's soul. As each shell became less stable due to his dark side energy, Sidious would simply transfer himself into another clone. This process was repeated several times<ref name="DE2" /> until the [[Battle of Onderon (Galactic Civil War)|death of his last clone]] on [[Onderon/Legends|Onderon]].<ref name="EE2">[[Empire's End 2|''Empire's End'' 2]]</ref>
*Dr. [[Cornelius Evazan/Legends|Cornelius Evazan]] invented a successful [[reanimation serum]].<ref name="GFCD">''[[Galaxy of Fear: City of the Dead]]''</ref>
*[[Darth Krayt]] managed to survive on borrowed time by preserving his body in a [[Stasis chamber/Legends|stasis chamber]] for decades. The side effects resulted in a gradual deterioration of his health, however.<ref name="Legacy15">[[Legacy (2006) 15|''Legacy'' (2006) 15]]</ref> But through a [[Battle on Had Abbadon|near-death experience]],<ref name="Legacy31">[[Legacy (2006) 31|''Legacy'' (2006) 31]]</ref> Krayt discovered<ref name="War6">[[Legacy — War 6|''Legacy — War'' 6]]</ref> the two powerful techniques of essence transfer and [[dark transfer]]; a dark side ability that could [[Force healing/Legends|heal]] virtually any injury,<ref name="LECG">''[[Legacy Era Campaign Guide]]''</ref> and thus enabled him to survive even death itself. His final death was achieved when the Jedi [[Cade Skywalker]] launched Krayt's body into [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant's]] [[Coruscant Prime/Legends|sun]].<ref name="War6" />
